correctness.rationale: The Gorenstein socle equals m^2 and is one-dimensional over k, so product on m/m² is nondegenerate symmetric B. Each nonzero v has exactly q lifts, and adjacency is B(v,w)=0. The q-1 nonzero socle elements are the unique universal graph vertices; other degrees are q^d-2 (isotropic v) or q^d-1 (nonisotropic v). Finite-field quadratic form classification distinguishes types by zero-count except in odd dimension where similarity class unique. Construction k+V+kz realizes all types; no coefficient field lift is assumed for the graph correspondence. Independently built small graphs and verified degree counts at q=2,3 in both parity types; all-q proof is algebraic.

originality.rationale: Both the 2026-10-13 graded ring reconstruction theorem and the stronger 2026-11-08 finite equicharacteristic Gorenstein theorem already prove precisely the degree distributions, graph-recovery of q,d and bilinear Witt type, and even ring isomorphism for the equicharacteristic family. The only explicit broader scope is mixed-characteristic rings, but Kadu already proves their multiplication pairing and orthogonality structure. Their graph is literally the same q-lift construction as the known equicharacteristic model R_B, so the submitted graph classification follows formally by transferring the earlier theorem. It does not introduce a new independently valuable graph invariant.
residual_risks: The decisive prior results cover standard/equicharacteristic forms directly; their implication for mixed-characteristic graphs relies on the elementary lifting of graph fibers, not a proved ring isomorphism.
Classification requires Gorenstein local, m³=0 !=m² and d>=3, and does not classify rings via graphs in mixed characteristic.
